Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 8, verse 1:

Naming of the surah

• It is called al-Anfal (the spoils of war), because it mentions al-anfal, which are the spoils (ghana'im) of the Battle of Badr, and their ruling. The word al-anfal does not occur in any other surah.

From the aims of the surah

• To explain the rulings on spoils of war, their distribution and their uses, and that the matter of these belongs to Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ). It also commands steadfastness in the religion, fear of Allah, and unity upon the truth.

• To mention the departure of the believers to the Battle of Badr, and Allah's kindness towards them: by reinforcing them with angels, strengthening them, pouring patience upon them, and supporting them with His great victory, which He made a criterion (furqan) between truth and falsehood.

• To point to what the believers are bound to observe: preparing their strength, keeping covenants, adhering to the principle of steadfastness whatever the enemy's numbers and equipment, and commanding unity of word and forbidding disputes.

• To explain the rulings of the treaty between the Muslims and the disbelievers, what follows from their breaking a covenant, and when peace is good; and to explain the rulings on prisoners of war, and the rulings on Muslims who remained behind in Makkah after the Hijrah, their guardianship (wilayah), and what follows from that guardianship.

[Tafsir]

They ask you, O Prophet, about the spoils on the day of Badr: how should you divide them among them? Say to them: Indeed, their matter belongs to Allah and His Messenger. The Messenger undertakes their division by the command of his Lord. So fear the punishment of Allah and do not proceed to disobey Him, leave off disputing and quarrelling over these properties, set right the state of affairs among you, and adhere to the obedience of Allah and His Messenger, if you are believers; for faith calls to obedience to Allah and His Messenger.

Truly, the believers in Allah are those whose hearts tremble with fear when Allah is mentioned, and when the verses of the Qur'an are recited to them, they increase in faith above the faith they already have, because they reflect on its meanings. They put their trust in Allah, the Exalted, so they hope in none other than Him and fear none other than Him.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 8, verse 3:

Those who persistently perform the prescribed prayers at their appointed times, and who spend from the wealth We have bestowed upon them in what We have commanded them to spend.

These are the ones who truly believe, outwardly and inwardly, in what Allah has revealed to them. They have high ranks with Allah, forgiveness for their sins, and generous provision, which is Paradise.

Just as you disagreed about the spoils of war, and God took them away from you and placed their distribution in the hands of Him and His Messenger (ﷺ), so too your Lord commanded you, O Prophet, to set out from Medina to meet the caravan of Quraysh, by the revelation that Jibril brought you, even though a group of the believers disliked going out.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 8, verse 6:

Some of the believers argue with you, O Prophet, about fighting, after it has become clear to them that it is certain to happen, as though they were being driven to death while looking right at it.

And remember, you who disputed, the promise of God to you of victory over one of the two groups: the caravan and what it carries of provisions, or the armed force, which is fighting the enemies and prevailing over them. You loved to have the caravan rather than the fighting. But God wills to establish the truth of Islam and raise it high by His command to you to fight the disbelievers, and to uproot the disbelievers by destruction.
So that Allah may establish Islam and its people, and eliminate polytheism and its people, even though the polytheists dislike that.

Remember the blessing of Allah upon you on the day of Badr, when you were seeking victory over your enemy. So Allah answered your supplication, saying: "I will reinforce you with a thousand of the angels, following one another."

And Allah did not make that reinforcement except as good news for you of victory, and so that your hearts might be reassured thereby, and that you might be certain of Allah's victory for you. Victory is only from Allah, not by the strength of your might or your power. Indeed, Allah is Almighty in His dominion, Wise in His management and His legislation.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 8, verse 11:

When Allah cast drowsiness upon you as a security from Him for you, from the fear of your enemy that they would overcome you, and sent down upon you water from the sky, purifying you with it from the minor impurities (al-ahdath al-zahira), and removing from you, inwardly, the whispers and thoughts of Satan, and to strengthen your hearts with patience at the time of fighting, and to make firm the feet of the believers by packing the sandy ground with rain so that feet would not slip in it.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 8, verse 12:

Remember, O Prophet, when your Lord revealed to the angels that He had sent to the believers at the Battle of Badr: "I am with you; I will support and help you. So strengthen the resolve of those who have believed. I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved, so strike [their] necks, O believers, and strike every fingertip and joint of them."

That which befell the disbelievers, of striking their heads, their necks, and their fingertips, is because they opposed Allah and His Messenger. And whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger, then indeed Allah is severe in punishment for him, in this world and in the Hereafter.

That is the punishment which I have hastened upon you, O disbelievers who oppose the commands of Allah and His Messenger in this world. So taste it in this worldly life, and for you in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire.

O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and acted by His law: when you meet those who disbelieve in battle, advancing toward you, do not turn your backs to them, fleeing from them; rather, stand firm against them, for Allah is with you and will give you victory over them.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 8, verse 16:

Whoever among you turns his back to them on the day of battle, except one who turns aside as a stratagem against the disbelievers, or one who withdraws to a company of the Muslims, then he has incurred anger from Allah, and his abode is Hell, and wretched is the destination.

Then you did not kill them, O believers, the disbelievers on the day of Badr; rather, it was God who killed them, as He helped you to do so. And you did not throw, when you threw, O Prophet; but it was God who threw, as He made the throw you threw reach the faces of the disbelievers. This was so that He might test the believers in God and His Messenger, and raise them through jihad to the highest ranks, and make them aware of His blessing upon them, so that they would thank Him, glorified is He, for that. Indeed God is All-Hearing of your supplications and your words, whether you conceal them or make them known, and All-Knowing of what is good for His servants.

This act of killing the polytheists and casting [the pebbles] at them when they fled, and the fair trial of granting the believers victory over their enemies, is from Allah to the believers. And [it is stated that] Allah, in what is yet to come, weakens and nullifies the scheming of the disbelievers until they are humbled and submit to the truth, or they are destroyed.

In the Tafsir al-Muyassar (King Fahd Complex), on Surah 8, verse 19:

If you (disbelievers) ask God to send down His might and punishment upon the transgressors and wrongdoers, then God has answered your request, when He inflicted upon you of His punishment that which was a deterrent for you and a lesson for the God-fearing. And if you (disbelievers) cease from disbelief in God and His Messenger, and from fighting His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), then it is better for you in your worldly life and in your Hereafter. And if you return to war and fighting Muhammad (ﷺ) and fighting his believing followers, We shall return you to defeat as you were defeated on the day of Badr, and your large numbers will avail you nothing, just as they did not avail you on the day of Badr, despite your great numbers and equipment and the small number and meager strength of the believers. And indeed, God is with the believers through His support and victory.

O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger, obey Allah and His Messenger in what He has commanded you and forbidden you, and do not turn away from obeying Allah and obeying His Messenger, while you hear what is recited to you of the Qur'an, its proofs and its evidences.

Do not be, O believers, in opposing Allah and His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), like the polytheists and the hypocrites who, when the Book of Allah is recited to them, say, "We have heard," with their ears, while in reality they do not ponder over what they have heard, nor do they reflect upon it.

Indeed, the most evil of creatures that crawl upon the earth in the sight of Allah are the deaf who have stopped their ears from hearing the truth, so they do not hear it, and the dumb who have had their tongues rendered incapable of speaking it, so they do not speak it. These are the ones who do not understand from Allah His command and His prohibition.

If Allah had known any good in these people, He would have made them hear the admonitions and lessons of the Qur'an, so that they would understand from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, His proofs and evidences. But Allah knows that there is no good in them and that they will not believe. And even if He had made them hear, by way of supposition and assumption, they would have turned away from faith deliberately and stubbornly after understanding it, for they are averse to it, with no inclination toward the truth in any way whatsoever.

O you who have believed in Allah as Lord and in Muhammad as Prophet and Messenger: respond to Allah and to the Messenger with obedience when he calls you to that which gives you life, that is, the truth. For in responding lies the reform of your lives in this world and in the Hereafter. And know, O believers, that Allah, exalted is He, is the One who disposes of all things, and He is able to come between a person and what his heart desires. So it is He, subhanahu, to whom response is due when He calls you, for in His hand is the dominion of everything. And know that you will be gathered on a Day about which there is no doubt, and He will recompense each soul according to what it deserves.

Beware, O believers, of a trial and affliction that will befall the wrongdoer and others alike. It will not be confined to the people of sin, nor to those who committed the sin directly; rather, it will strike the righteous along with them if they were able to forbid the wrongdoing and did not do so. And know that Allah is severe in punishment toward whoever opposes His command and His prohibition.

Remember, O believers, the blessings of God upon you when you were in Mecca, few in number and oppressed, fearing that its disbelievers would snatch you away swiftly. Then He provided for you a refuge to which you could retreat, which is Medina, and strengthened you with His help against them on the day of Badr, and provided you with good things (tayyibat), among which were the spoils of war, so that you might give thanks to Him for what He has provided you and bestowed upon you.

O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and acted by His law, do not betray Allah and His Messenger by abandoning what Allah has made obligatory upon you or by doing what He has forbidden you, and do not neglect what Allah has entrusted to you, while you know that it is a trust that must be fulfilled.

Know, O believers, that your wealth, over which God has made you successors, and your children, whom God has granted you, are a trial and a test from God for His servants, to see whether they will be thankful to Him for them and obey Him through them, or whether they will be preoccupied with them and turn away from Him. And know that with God is what is better, and a great reward, for those who fear Him and obey Him.

O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and acted according to His law: if you fear Allah by carrying out His commands and avoiding His prohibitions, He will grant you a criterion (furqan) between truth and falsehood, will erase from you your past sins and cover them over, and will not hold you accountable for them. And Allah is the Possessor of great bounty and abundant, far-reaching giving.

Remember, O Messenger, when the disbelievers of your people in Makkah plotted against you, to imprison you, kill you, or expel you from your land. They plotted, but Allah turned back their scheming upon them as a recompense for them. Allah also plans, and Allah is the best of planners; He punishes them for their scheming in a way they do not perceive.

When the verses of the Mighty Qur'an are recited to those who disbelieve in Allah, they say, out of ignorance and stubborn opposition to the truth: "We have already heard this before. If we wished, we could say the like of this Qur'an. This is nothing but the fables of the ancients, which you recite to us, O Messenger."

Remember, O Messenger, the words of the polytheists among your people when they prayed, "O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky, or bring us a painful torment."
Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, would not punish these polytheists while you, O Messenger, are among them, and Allah would not punish them while they are seeking forgiveness for their sins.

How could they not deserve the punishment of Allah, when they bar His allies, the believers, from circumambulating the Ka'bah and from praying in the Sacred Mosque? They were not its guardians (awliya'). The guardians of Allah are none other than those who are mindful of Him (yattaqunahu) by performing His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions. But most of the disbelievers do not know; therefore they claimed for themselves a matter that others are more entitled to.

Their prayer at the Sacred Mosque was nothing but whistling and clapping. So taste the punishment of killing and capture on the Day of Badr, because of your disbelief and your deeds, which none would commit except the disbelievers who deny the Oneness of their Lord and the message of their Prophet.

Indeed, those who disbelieved, denying the oneness of God and disobeying His Messenger, spend their wealth and give it to their like among the polytheists and people of misguidance; so that they may turn people away from the way of God and prevent the believers from faith in God and His Messenger. Thus they will spend their wealth in that, and then the outcome of that expenditure will be regret and anguish for them, because their wealth will go to waste, and they will not attain what they hope for of extinguishing the light of God and barring people from His path. Then, in the end, the believers will defeat them. And those who disbelieved will be gathered to Hell, where they will be punished.

Allah will gather them, and He will disgrace those who disbelieved in their Lord and spent their wealth to prevent people from believing in Allah and to bar them from His path. This is so that Allah may distinguish the wicked from the good. He will make the unlawful wealth that was spent to bar people from the religion of Allah pile up, one part upon another, and He will throw it into the Fire of Hell. Those disbelievers are the losers in this world and in the Hereafter.

Say, O Messenger, to those who disbelieved in the Oneness of God among your people, the polytheists: if they desist from disbelief and hostility toward the Prophet (ﷺ), and return to faith in God alone and refrain from fighting the Messenger and the believers, then God will forgive them what has passed of sins, for Islam (submission to God) effaces what came before it. But if these polytheists return to fighting you, O Messenger, after the defeat you inflicted upon them on the day of Badr, then the way of the earlier peoples has already passed: that when they denied and persisted in their obstinacy, We hastened to punish them with torment and retribution.

Fight them, O believers, until there is no more shirk and no more barring from the path of Allah, and until none is worshipped except Allah alone, without partner, so that the trial (fitnah) upon the servants of Allah on earth is lifted, and so that religion, obedience and worship are entirely for Allah, sincerely devoted to Him alone, to the exclusion of anything else. But if they desist from persecuting the believers and from associating partners with Allah, and turn to the true religion alongside you, then Allah does not conceal from Himself what they do of abandoning disbelief and entering Islam.

And if these polytheists turn away from what you, O believers, have called them to—faith in Allah and His Messenger and ceasing to fight you—and they refuse except to persist in disbelief and in fighting you, then know that Allah is your helper and your supporter against them. How excellent a helper and supporter He is for you and for His allies against your enemies.

Know, O believers, that whatever spoils you have taken from your enemy through jihad in the cause of Allah, one-fifth of it belongs to God and to the Messenger, and the remaining four-fifths belong to the fighters who were present at the battle. The remaining fifth is divided into five portions. The first is for Allah and His Messenger, to be spent on the general interests of the Muslims. The second is for the close relatives of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), namely the Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib; this fifth was assigned to them in place of charity, since charity is not lawful for them. The third is for the orphans whose fathers have died while they are still below the age of puberty. The fourth is for the needy (al-masakin) who do not possess what suffices them and meets their need. The fifth is for the traveller who has been cut off from his provisions. This applies if you truly affirm the Oneness of Allah, obey Him, and believe in what He sent down to His servant Muhammad (ﷺ) of signs, aid, and victory on the day when He distinguished between truth and falsehood at Badr, the day when the two hosts met: the host of the believers and the host of the polytheists. And Allah is over all things capable, nothing can frustrate Him.

Remember when you were on the nearer side of the valley to Madinah, while the enemy was on the farther side of the valley, and the caravan was lower than you toward the coast of the Red Sea. Had you arranged a meeting with them, you would have disagreed about it. But Allah brought you together without prior appointment, so that He might accomplish a matter that was decreed to be done: the victory of His allies and the humiliation of His enemies through killing and capture. This was so that whoever was destroyed among them would be destroyed after a clear proof from Allah had been established against him, which he witnessed and which cut off his excuse, and so that whoever lived would live after a proof from Allah had been established and made manifest to him. Indeed Allah is All-Hearing of the words of both groups, nothing is hidden from Him, and He is All-Knowing of their intentions and their deeds.

Commemorate, O Prophet, when Allah showed you in your dream that the number of your enemy was small. You informed the believers of that, and their hearts were strengthened, and they became bold to fight them. Had your Lord shown you that their number was large, your companions would have hesitated to face them, and you would have become cowardly and disputed among yourselves about the matter of fighting. But Allah protected you from failure and saved you from the consequence of that. Indeed, He is Knowing of the hidden contents of hearts and the natures of souls.

Remember also when the enemy appeared to you at the battlefield and you saw them as few, so you became bold against them, and He made you appear few in their eyes, so that they would neglect preparing for your fighting, that Allah might accomplish a matter that was (already) decreed to be done, so that Allah's promise of victory and triumph to you would be fulfilled. Thus the word of Allah became the highest, and the word of those who disbelieved became the lowest. And to Allah is the return of all matters, so He will recompense each (party) according to what it deserves.

O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and acted by His law: when you encounter a group of the people of disbelief who have prepared themselves to fight you, then stand firm and do not turn your backs to flee from them, and remember Allah abundantly, calling upon Him and earnestly beseeching Him to send down victory upon you and success over your enemy, so that you may prevail.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 8, verse 46:

Hold fast to obedience to Allah and obedience to His Messenger in all your circumstances, and do not dispute with one another, lest you lose heart and your strength and your victory depart. And be steadfast when you meet the enemy. Indeed, Allah is with those who are patient, with help, victory and support, and He will never forsake them.

Do not be like the polytheists who went out from their homes out of arrogance and to be seen by people, in order to prevent others from entering the religion of Allah. And Allah encompasses what they do; nothing of it is hidden from Him.

Remember when Satan made their deeds seem fair to the disbelievers, and said to them: "No one will overcome you today, and I am your ally." Then when the two hosts came in sight of each other, the disbelievers with Satan and the Muslims with the angels, he turned on his heels and said to the disbelievers: "I am free of you. I see what you do not see; I fear Allah." So he forsook them and disowned them. And Allah is severe in punishment toward whoever disobeys Him and does not repent with sincere repentance.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 8, verse 49:

And remember, [O Muslims], when the people of doubt and hypocrisy and those with sickness in their hearts were saying, seeing the small number of the Muslims and the great number of their enemy: "These Muslims have been deluded by their religion, and so it has led them into this peril." But these hypocrites did not realize that whoever puts his trust in Allah and relies on His promise, then Allah will not forsake him, for Allah is Mighty, nothing can overpower Him, and Wise in His management and His creation.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 8, verse 50:

If you could see, O Messenger, the state of the angels taking the souls of the disbelievers and tearing them out, while they strike their faces when they come forward and strike their backs when they flee, and say to them: ﴿Taste the punishment of burning,﴾ you would see a dreadful matter. Although the context of this verse was occasioned by the battle of Badr, it is general in application to every disbeliever.

That punishment which befell you, O disbelievers, is because of your evil deeds in the life of this world. And Allah does not wrong anyone among His creatures even the weight of an atom; rather, He is the Just Judge who does not oppress.

Indeed, what befell the disbelievers on that day is the way of God in punishing the tyrants of earlier nations, such as Pharaoh and those before him, when they denied God's messengers and rejected His signs. So God sent down His punishment upon them because of their sins. Indeed, God is Mighty, not overcome, severe in punishment toward whoever disobeys Him and does not repent of his sin.

That punishment is because God does not change a blessing He has bestowed upon a people until they change what is in themselves, turning their good condition into a bad one. God hears the words of His creatures and knows their circumstances, and He brings upon them what His knowledge and will have decreed.

The condition of these disbelievers in this matter is like the condition of the people of Pharaoh, who denied Moses, and like the condition of those before them who denied their messengers, so Allah destroyed them because of their sins, and drowned the people of Pharaoh in the sea. Each of them had been doing what was not right for them to do: denying the messengers of Allah, rejecting His signs, and associating others with Him in worship.

Indeed, the most evil of the creatures that crawl upon the earth in the sight of Allah are the disbelievers who persist in disbelief. They do not believe in the messengers of Allah, they do not acknowledge His oneness, and they do not follow His law.

Among those wicked ones are the Jews who entered into treaties with you, agreeing not to fight against you nor to support anyone against you, yet they break their covenant time after time, and they do not fear Allah.

If you encounter these people who break covenants and pacts in battle, then inflict upon them such punishment as will strike terror into the hearts of those behind them and scatter their gatherings, so that they may take heed and not dare to do what those before them did.

If you, O Messenger, fear treachery from a people, its signs having appeared, then throw back to them their covenant, so that both parties are equal in knowing that there is no covenant after today. Indeed, Allah does not love those who betray in their covenants, who break the pact and the agreement.
Let not those who denied the signs of Allah suppose that they have escaped and gotten away, or that Allah is unable to overpower them. Indeed, they will not escape the punishment of Allah.

And prepare against them, O believers, whatever force and equipment you are able to muster, so that you may strike terror into the enemies of God and your enemies, who lie in wait for you, and frighten others besides them whose enmity is not apparent to you now, but God knows them and knows what they conceal. And whatever you spend of wealth or otherwise in the cause of God, whether little or much, God will replace it for you in this world, and will store up its reward for you until the Day of Resurrection, and you will not be wronged in the least in the reward for it.
And if they incline to peace, then incline to it too, and put your trust in Allah. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing of what they say, the All-Knowing of their intentions.

"And if they intend to deceive you, then indeed Allah is sufficient for you against their deception. It is He who supported you with His help and with the believers, from the Muhajirun and the Ansar, and who joined their hearts together after dispersion. Had you spent all that is in the earth to join their hearts, you could not have joined them, but Allah joined them together through faith, so they became brothers, loving one another. Indeed, He is Almighty in His dominion, Wise in His command and His management."

"And if they intend to deceive you, then indeed Allah is sufficient for you against their deception. It is He who supported you with His help and with the believers, from the Muhajirun and the Ansar, and who joined their hearts together after dispersion. Had you spent all that is in the earth to join their hearts, you could not have joined them, but Allah joined them together through faith, so they became brothers, loving one another. Indeed, He is Almighty in His dominion, Wise in His command and His management."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 8, verse 64:

﴿O Prophet, Allah is sufficient for you, and sufficient for those believers who follow you, against the evil of your enemies.﴾

O Prophet, urge the believers to fight. If there are twenty among you who are steadfast when meeting the enemy, they will overcome two hundred of them; and if there are one hundred among you who are steadfast, they will overcome a thousand of the disbelievers, for they are a people who lack understanding and comprehension of what Allah has prepared for those who strive in His cause. They fight for worldly dominance over the earth and for corruption therein.

Now Allah has lightened [the burden] upon you, O believers, because of the weakness within you. So if there are among you one hundred steadfast, they will overcome two hundred of the disbelievers, and if there are among you one thousand, they will overcome two thousand of them, by the permission of Allah. And Allah is with the steadfast, by His support and His victory.

It is not fitting for a Prophet to have captives from among his enemies until he has thoroughly engaged in killing, so as to instill terror in their hearts and to firmly establish the pillars of the religion. You, O believers, by taking ransom from the captives of Badr, desire the goods of this world, while Allah desires the manifestation of His religion, through which the Hereafter is attained. Allah is Mighty, none can overpower Him, and Wise in His legislation.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 8, verse 68:

Had there not been a decree from Allah that had already preceded, through the predestination and divine decree, permitting the spoils of war and the ransoming of captives for this Ummah, a great punishment would have befallen you because of your taking the spoils and the ransom before a legislative ruling had been revealed concerning them.

Then eat of the spoils of war that you have taken, and of the ransom for the captives, for it is lawful and good. And be mindful of the rulings of Allah's religion and His legislation. Indeed, Allah is Most Forgiving toward His servants, Most Merciful to them.

O Prophet, say to those captives you have taken at Badr: Do not grieve over the ransom that was taken from you. If Allah knows that there is any good in your hearts, He will give you better than what was taken from you of wealth, by making easy for you from His bounty abundant good, and He will forgive you your sins. Allah is All-Forgiving to His servants' sins when they repent, and Most Merciful to them. (Allah has fulfilled His promise to al-'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, and others.)

If those whom you have released as prisoners, O Prophet, intend to betray you again, then do not despair. They had already betrayed God before, and fought against you, so God gave you victory over them. God is All-Knowing of what the breasts conceal, All-Wise in the management of the affairs of His servants.

The Noble Qur'an verse 8:72 is quoted in the commentary; here is the translation of the passage.

Indeed, those who believed in Allah and His Messenger, and acted according to His law, and emigrated to the abode of Islam, or to a land where they can freely worship their Lord, and strove in the way of Allah with their wealth and their lives, and those who sheltered the emigrants in their homes and comforted them with their wealth, and supported the religion of Allah: these are allies of one another. As for those who believed but did not emigrate from the abode of disbelief, you are not obligated to protect and support them until they emigrate. And if they are wronged by the disbelievers and seek your support, then you must come to their aid, except against a people with whom you have a binding treaty that they have not broken. And Allah is Seeing of what you do, and He rewards each according to the intention and deed.

Those who disbelieve are allies of one another. And if you, O believers, do not become allies of one another, there will be strife on earth and great corruption, through turning people away from the path of Allah and strengthening the pillars of disbelief.

Those who believed in Allah and His Messenger, emigrated from their homes seeking the abode of Islam, or a land where they could freely worship their Lord, and strove to make the word of Allah supreme; and those who gave refuge to their emigrant brothers, sheltered them, and comforted them with wealth and support: these are the truly believing ones. For them is forgiveness for their sins and a generous, abundant provision in the Gardens of Bliss.

Those who believed after them, and emigrated and struggled alongside you in the cause of God, they are of you, O believers. They have the same rights as you and bear the same obligations as you. And blood relatives are more entitled to one another in inheritance, by the judgment of God, than the general body of Muslims. Indeed God has knowledge of everything; He knows what is good for His servants in terms of some of them inheriting from others through kinship and lineage, rather than inheriting through alliance (al-hilf), and other matters that existed at the beginning of Islam.
